title: Linux.Ngioweb_Botnet_Investigation_eb2
description: Investigate and contain potential botnet activity on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns, with multiple systems generating excessive outbound connections. Initial analysis suggests potential botnet activity. Your task is to investigate and contain this activity.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host `victim` with credentials:
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

From this host, you can access other systems in the network as needed.

Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host `victim` with credentials:
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

From this host, you can access other systems in the network as needed.

Enter the passkey 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external command-and-control server?
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, check running services and look for unusual network connections. The service name can be found by examining systemd services and their associated network activity.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for unusual network connections.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or those that are not part of the standard system services.

levels.title: Identify Excessive Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating excessive network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine systemd timers and services for unusual activity. The service name can be found by checking systemd timers and their associated network traffic.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd timers and services for unusual activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are associated with services generating high network traffic.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services that start automatically. The persistence mechanism can be found by examining systemd timers and services.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers and services that start automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled` to list all enabled unit files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for unit files that are associated with the suspicious service.
